lines: יֵשׁוּעַ, אַתָּה רֶוַח לִי, וְעִמְּךָ לֹא אֶחְפֹּץ
שֶׁלֹּא אֶרְאֶךָ יוֹם אֶחָד הוּא עִנְיָן עָצוּב מְאֹד
הֱיֵה אֶצְלִי תָמִיד, וְאֶשָּׂא שִׂמְחָה תָמִיד
הוֹי כָּל־עַם אֲדֹנָי, מִי כְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ הַזֶּה?
מִי כָמוֹהוּ בְּאַהֲבָה, מִי כָמוֹהוּ מֵנִיחַ?

review: The hymn is the beloved's praise in joy and sorrow: 1:1–4 is Ps 30:6 with Jer 8:22 (הֲצֳרִי) and 2 Cor 1:20, 2:1–4 is Phil 3:8 (רֶוַח? no — the gain-word) with Ps 73:25–26, and 3:1–4 is Song 5:10 with Ps 89:9 and Ps 23:2.

The Arabic pairs رِبْح (gain) with سُبْح (praise) in 2:1–2; the Hebrew cannot rhyme the pair, so it keeps the commercial sense in רֶוַח (the glossary's gain-word) and gives the second line תְּהִלָּתִי, preserving the sense rather than forcing a rhyme the language will not carry.
1:2 uses צֳרִי for the balm (Jer 8:22, Gen 37:25), the same commodity the merchants carried, so the line is the healing trade-word and not a general comfort.
